    Features

    Every Archie feature, by area

    179 features in 18 areas. Each one opens to where it is in Archie, how to use it, and its limits.

    179 features

    Talking to your agent

    • Stop a reply partway

      Type stop, or press Stop under the reply, while your agent is working; what it already finished stays done and nothing more happens.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.5
    • Tables and checklists in replies

      In Archie, your agent can answer with a table or a checklist when that is the clearer shape, and links and code show properly.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • New chat

      Press New chat and your agent starts fresh. It forgets the conversation and keeps what it has learned about you.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Question cards keep their buttons

      The cards where your agent offers choices keep working for two weeks, even after Archie restarts, so a card from Friday still answers on Monday.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • What your agent saved and looked at

      Under a reply, Archie says what your agent saved to your lists, with Open and Undo, and what it read to answer.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Ask your agent ordinary questions

      Your agent answers ordinary questions the way any AI chat does, such as how to word a hard email, in the same conversation as everything else it does.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Your agent looks back through your conversation

      Your agent keeps the last twenty messages in front of it. Ask about something from further back and it searches your conversation for it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Search this chat

      Type a word or a name and Archie shows every message in your chat with an agent that has all of them, newest first. Press one to go to it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Charts in the conversation

      Ask for a chart and your agent draws it in the conversation as bars, a line or a pie, with the numbers on it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • The Today line over the message box

      One line over the message box says what changed and what went out today, like "Today: 4 changes, 1 sent". Press it for the list, each change with Open and Undo.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Not now, answered at once

      Press Not now, No thanks, Skip or Cancel under something your agent offered, and Archie answers "Okay, left it." right away, without asking the AI, and drops what the card offered.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Your presses, shown as presses

      A button you press shows on your side of the chat as that button, pressed, over the first words of the card it answered. Confirm says the change it confirms, and a press never changes your agent's words.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Replies in your lists' own words

      Your agent names a change by the column's name on your list, like For. It says what it did, like "I looked it up online", and leaves out Archie's own words, such as skill and specialist. Who's Got This keeps its list as Who has what.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Unasked messages wait for the answer

      Messages your agent sends without being asked, like the morning list, a card about new mail or a routine's report, wait until it has finished answering you.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Unasked messages say so

      When your agent sends something without being asked, a line over it says so and what it is, like "Sent on its own at 6:30 AM: your morning list."

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Links Archie never read are cut back

      If a reply holds a web link to a site Archie never read or found in a search, the link is cut back to the site's front page.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • /pending moves waiting cards down

      Type /pending and everything still waiting on you is posted again at the bottom of the chat. The earlier copy says the newest card replaced it, and its buttons go.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Suggested asks in an empty chat

      An empty chat suggests up to three things you can ask your agent right now, picked from the skills it has and the accounts you connected. Tap one and it goes as if you had typed it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12

    Voice

    • Say a message instead of typing

      Press the microphone beside the message box to speak a message; Archie turns it into words on your computer, and only the words go to your AI company.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Spoken replies on iMessage come as audio messages

      On iMessage, when your agent answers out loud, the answer comes as an audio message in the Messages thread, instead of a file to open somewhere else.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12

    Your phone

    • Archie Mobile

      Archie Mobile, for iPhone and Android, reaches the agent on your computer, which locks every message with a key that only your phone also holds.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Your agent on iMessage, with its own Apple ID

      On a Mac, your agent answers in iMessage in the chat you have with yourself, with its name on its replies, or on an Apple ID of its own.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.6
    • Notifications on Archie Mobile

      Turn on notifications in Archie Mobile and your phone shows reminders, reports, new mail, and replies to what you sent from it, even with the app closed.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • A phone message waits for a sleeping computer

      A message sent from Archie Mobile while your computer sleeps waits and says so, and your agent answers it when the computer wakes, knowing it was sent earlier.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.5
    • Run a routine or tune a skill from your phone

      From Archie Mobile you can run a routine now, pick a skill's Response quality, and switch a skill's scheduled messages off and on.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.5
    • More of your agent's setup from your phone

      From Archie Mobile you can let in or block someone who messaged your agent, turn on calls to businesses, and paste your AI account's key. You can also change what Email Manager and Text Replies watch for, and say whose each mail account is.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12
    • Short answers on your phone

      Text your agent from your phone and it answers in the first line and keeps the reply short, with no headings.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • When your chat app stops reaching your agent

      If messages on your chat app stop reaching your agent for more than half an hour, Archie tells you in Archie, and so on Archie Mobile, with what to do on the computer. It says so again once they get through.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12

    Email

    • Email goes out when you send it or set a time

      Your agent drafts email replies and can't send one on its own. Each draft comes to your chat as a card with Send on it, and nothing leaves your account until you send it or set a time for it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • Edit a draft in a pop-up

      Press Edit it on an email or text draft and a pop-up shows the message it answers. It has three ways to change the draft: type it your way, tell your agent what to change, or have it write three more.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Drafts waiting for you to press Send

      Every draft card says "Not sent yet." while it waits. Over the message box, a line such as "2 waiting to send" counts the drafts in this conversation, and pressing it opens the list.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Write like me

      Turn on Write like me and give it some of your own writing: your sent mail, a document, or something you paste. When your agent drafts a reply, in chat, to mail that just arrived, or to a text, it writes it the way you write, and a text still reads like a text. You still read every draft before it goes.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Text Replies on a Mac

      On a Mac, your agent reads texts as they arrive in Messages and offers a reply on a card when one needs an answer. Nothing sends until you press Send, and a reply goes out from your own number, as if you had typed it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.4
    • Keep for every draft

      When you type your brokerage, phone number, or business name into a blank on an email draft, the card offers Keep for every draft.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Stop watching your inbox

      When your agent starts reading your mail, it says in the chat which inboxes it reads and how often, with a Stop watching button.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Mail from people you write to comes first

      Mail from someone you wrote to in the last two weeks is read at once; other mail can wait a few minutes, which lowers what your AI account is charged.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Blanks in a draft

      Your agent leaves a blank in square brackets, like [her school], for a detail nobody gave, and an email or text with a blank in it will not send.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Check before sending

      On an email your agent drafts in chat, a price, a day, or a time that nobody gave it is listed under the draft for you to check.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • First text to a lead

      Ask your agent to text a lead, and it writes the text, says whether they agreed to texts, and puts a button under it so you can send it yourself.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Known senders

      Before your agent reads an email, Archie checks whether you have the sender written down on your lists, on your agent, in what you have told your agent about your work, or as someone you wrote to lately.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.13
    • An email offers the change to your list

      When an email says something new about an entry on one of your lists, your agent puts the change on a card, and nothing changes until you press Update.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.1
    • A price nobody gave is left as a blank

      If a draft quotes a price not in what you typed, your lists, your files, or the email it answers, it is left in brackets and Send waits.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.13
    • A sent draft says it went

      Your agent's own words are never changed. When you press Send on an email it drafted, Archie says it went under the message that came with the draft: "Sent to Ace Septic at 8:01am."

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11

    Calendar

    • Approve a calendar change

      When your agent wants to add, move or delete an event on a calendar you connected, it shows you the exact change and makes it only after you approve it in a later message. The exception is Yes, and stop asking, for some changes to your own calendar.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • Your calendar is checked before a reply about a time

      When a text or an email asks about a time, your agent looks at your calendar before it writes the reply, so the draft won't say yes to a time you're already booked. When it offers to put something on your calendar, it tells you if that time is already taken.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.5
    • Invitations and a place on an event

      When your agent sets up a meeting, it can put the place on it and invite people once you say yes. The change it shows you first names everyone who will get an invitation, by name and email address.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Ask what's on, what's due, or what's free

      Ask about some days and Archie hands your agent what your lists, your calendar, and your reminders hold for those days before it answers.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Dates from your lists on the Calendar

      The Calendar tab shows the dates on your lists beside your calendar events, reminders, and routines, so a booking kept on a list shows on its day.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A stop moved onto a busy day

      Move a stop to a day its truck or driver is on your calendar for something else, or a day that job already has a stop. Your agent tells you what is there and asks before moving it.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Where Bookings and your calendar differ

      On an event trailer agent, the morning list compares your Bookings list with your calendar for today and the next two weeks, and says where one has a booking the other does not. Ask what is on a day and your agent says the same.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11

    Lists and to-dos

    • Your to-do list on the Dashboard

      Your to-do list is the first thing on your agent's Dashboard, where you can tick something off or add one without asking your agent.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.3
    • Stages on a list

      A list can show its steps, like Quoted, Booked, Out and Picked up, with each entry's step in color and a count at each step.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Lists in the sidebar and on the Dashboard

      Keep up to six lists in your agent's sidebar, under Jobs, and each one shows on the Dashboard with its count and where its entries stand.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Lists made from what you tell your agent

      When you first set up your agent and say what work you do, it drafts up to three lists that work runs on, with their steps.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Where you keep your work

      The last of your agent's first questions is where you keep your work today, with a button for each place, and its goodbye offers a way to bring in each of the first two.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Bring in a spreadsheet someone emailed

      Say "bring in the spreadsheet Dana emailed", and your agent finds the email, opens the file, and puts its rows on a card for you to add.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Who owes you money

      Ask who owes you money, and your agent answers from entries on your lists marked billed and not paid, oldest first, with the days each has waited.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Fixing a save your agent claimed but never made

      If a reply says it put something on your lists and nothing was saved, Archie adds a line saying so, with Save it to save it now.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A new list takes its first entries

      Ask for a new list and say what goes on it in the same message, and your agent makes the list and adds those entries in one reply.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Who to call

      Ask your agent who to call, and Archie works it out from your People and Deals lists: birthdays, closing anniversaries, quiet leads, and past clients.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Maybe already on a list

      When your agent adds someone, Archie looks on your lists for the same phone number, email, or name, and your agent says who it may be.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Hear when a booking puts something in two places

      When a booking puts a trailer or a unit in two places on the same day, Archie saves it as asked and says which booking it runs into.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Bring a spreadsheet into a list

      Import a spreadsheet into one of your lists. Archie matches the columns, leaves out rows already there, and names every cell it could not read.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Drop a spreadsheet in the chat

      Drop a spreadsheet into the chat and Archie puts up a card that names the list it fits and how many rows would come in.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Check new entries on one card before Add

      Hand your agent a photo, a page, or your calendar, and every entry it finds for one of your lists goes on one card you check before anything is added.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Bring a shared Google Sheet into a list

      Ask your agent to bring a Google Sheet you shared with it into one of your lists. The rows come in on a card you check first.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • How far along a list is

      Tell Archie about how many a list will hold, and it shows how many are entered so far, such as 25 of about 300 units entered.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Fold a row listed twice into one

      When a unit number or another value meant to be on a list once shows up twice, the list says so, and Review keeps the row you pick.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Ask about a unit by number

      Ask about unit 31 and your agent finds the row titled S-31, matching names like Trailer 4 or INV-1042 by their letters and numbers.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Keep a list matched to its spreadsheet

      Keep your own spreadsheet, and the list you brought in from it stays matched: Archie changes the list when you save the file, never changes your file, and asks before taking an entry off.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • A late pickup, asked about once a day

      Archie asks you about a late pickup for a rental at most once a day in the same chat, unless you bring that rental up.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Matching entries, added up in code

      When Archie looks up entries on one of your lists and two or more match, code adds up the number columns, like units and price. Your agent gets the totals, so it does not add them itself.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Units out, counted place by place

      When Archie looks up the units you have out, code counts them place by place against the rentals running there today. Your agent hears where your two lists agree, where they differ, and by how many.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11

    Routines and reminders

    • Reminders on the to-do list

      A reminder you ask for also goes on your to-do list; tick it off and the reminder is not said, and deleting it in one place removes both.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Remind me later

      When a reminder goes off, Remind me later offers in an hour, this evening or tomorrow, each with its time on the button, or another time in your words.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Your agent works while you are away

      Your agent runs routines, reads new mail, and reports to you with nobody watching, for as many hours as your computer is on and Archie is open.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Morning list

      For a line of work Archie has a setup for, your agent can send what is on today each morning, built from your lists without asking an AI.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Waking the computer for a routine

      A routine set for seven in the morning arrives at seven, even if your computer was asleep. Archie wakes it a few minutes before, runs it, and lets it sleep.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Missed routines run when the computer wakes

      A routine due while your computer was asleep runs when it wakes, as long as that is the same morning, afternoon, or evening. Past that, its row says it missed.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • One routine at several times a day

      A routine can run at several set times a day, up to 24, like 9:00 in the morning and 5:00 in the afternoon.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Reminders

      Tell your agent to remind you at a time, and it does, in your own words, at that minute, without asking an AI anything to read it back.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • A reminder that stands down when the person writes back

      Make a reminder conditional, like "remind me Thursday to chase the quote unless Ellen has replied". If Ellen emails or texts in first, it is dropped and Archie tells you.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Alerts on your computer

      When your agent posts on its own, like a reminder or a routine's report, your computer shows an alert with the agent's name and the first line.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.5
    • Evening question offer

      A day after your first evening, an agent with the journal offers once to ask you one question about your day at 9:30pm, and your answer goes in the journal.

      • On your computer
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.3.13
    • Today's Calendar skips an empty day

      On a morning with nothing on your calendar, the store's Today's Calendar routine sends nothing and uses none of your AI. Press Run now and it still answers.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11

    Memory and knowledge

    • Knowledge as folders

      The Knowledge tab opens like folders: Documents your agent reads, Lists it keeps up to date, Memory, and How you write.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.3
    • Your agent's first questions

      When you first open Archie, your agent asks a few questions about your work, starting with the first thing you say, so it can help you better.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • What your agent keeps

      At the top of an agent's Knowledge tab, Archie counts its lists, documents, and things it remembers about you, and shows the latest list changes with Undo.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • What your agent remembers about you

      Your agent keeps a short list of what it has learned about you. You can read every line, add one, change one, or delete one.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Bring in what ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini knows about you

      Archie gives you one sentence to send ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Paste its answer back, tick the lines to keep, and your agent remembers them.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Saved to memory line

      When your agent saves a note to its memory, a line under its reply names the note, with Open and Undo.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12
    • Your small files, checked for what you ask

      When you ask about something, Archie looks through your small files, like a price sheet or a page of notes, for lines that mention it, and hands them to your agent before it answers. No extra AI call is made.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11

    Files and pictures

    • Send files to your agent, and get files back

      Send your agent photos, a video, a recording or a document in Archie, and it sends files it made back the same way.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Read PDFs that are scans

      Some PDFs are photographs of a page, such as a scanned statement, a signed contract or a fax, so the file holds no words to read. Switch this on and Archie looks at the pages and writes out what is on them.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • The page an answer came from

      Ask where a figure came from and your agent can name the page: Archie reads a PDF you gave it as numbered pages, so you can open that page yourself.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Your whole agent in one backup file

      Everything you built goes in one file you save where you like, with no key or token in it. Archie can save one every week.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.2
    • Your agent saves real files

      Your agent writes the actual file, such as a PDF, a Word file, a spreadsheet or a deck, and tells you where it put it.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • PDF reports with charts

      Ask for a PDF and your agent lays it out on your computer, with headings, bullets, page breaks, and real bar, line or pie charts drawn in.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • PowerPoint decks you can change

      Ask for a deck and you get a real PowerPoint file you can open and change, with each heading starting a slide.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Change a spreadsheet, Word file or deck you give it

      Give your agent a spreadsheet, Word file, deck or text file and ask for a change. Once you confirm, it sends back a changed copy in the same style.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.10
    • Your agent makes pictures

      Your agent can make a picture and send it to you in the conversation, drawn with OpenAI or Google on your own account.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • A file opened from an email comes into the chat

      After your agent opens a file attached to an email, ask for it, like "send me that invoice", and the file itself comes into the conversation you are in. Files your agent sends go out as big as each chat app takes.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12

    Websites and apps

    • Your agent uses websites

      With no direct connection, your agent can use a website itself in a browser window on your computer: it reads, clicks and types, and you can watch.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Practice runs on a website

      Send your agent to look around a site before it does anything real there. It clicks through, finishes nothing, and notes how the site is laid out for next time.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Flight check-in

      Your agent finds the flight in your confirmation email, checks in on the airline's site the day before, takes a free seat, and sends you the boarding pass.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Your agent uses apps on a Mac

      On a Mac, your agent can use the apps you allow, such as Numbers or Preview, without moving your pointer. If you start using that app, it waits for you.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.4
    • Buying on a website

      Your agent can buy things for you on a website, if you switch that on. It is off until you do. You choose the shops it may buy from, the most it may spend on one order, and the most in total over 1, 7, 14 or 30 days. The limit is checked against the price it reads on the page.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Your agent phones a business

      With Call businesses switched on, your agent can phone a business for you, to ask its hours or prices or whether it can fit you in. It shows you the call first, on a card, and nothing dials until you press Place the call.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Finding places on the map

      Ask for somewhere to eat near the office open at eight, and your agent looks it up on the map: name, street, distance, phone number and hours.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Prices at Shopify stores

      Ask Price Watch to check your prices, and your agent looks up what Shopify stores charge right now, whether it is in stock, and a link to that store's checkout.

      • On your computer
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.3.1

    Skills and the store

    • Your agent takes on the jobs you pick

      Each agent carries only the add-ons you put on it, so it fits the way you work and a reply costs less than carrying every one.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Every add-on is included

      Every skill, routine, specialist and personality in the store comes with Archie, with no price of its own.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.2
    • Archie asks before an add-on goes on

      Whenever you add an add-on, anywhere in Archie, Archie asks first. It shows the add-on, the agent it is going on, what it will use, and which of those accounts that agent already has connected. Then you press Install, or Cancel.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.2
    • Written setups for four lines of work

      Tell Archie you rent portable restrooms or event restroom trailers, run a home trades company, or sell homes, and it starts with that work's lists and a few rules.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A written setup for lead generation

      Tell Archie your business sells leads, calls or booked appointments, and it starts with Clients, Sources and Orders lists and rules about consent and promises to clients.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Job Hunt shows where the people you know work

      Drop in the connections file LinkedIn emails you and Job Hunt shows where the people you know work now, then drafts a note to the right one.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.3.10
    • Add-ons bring no code

      An add-on is a text file your agent reads: written instructions plus settings. It brings no code of its own, and nothing in it runs as a program.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Ask whether your agent can do something

      Ask your agent whether it can do something, and it searches the Marketplace's add-ons for one that fits, or offers to write a new skill when none does.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Write a skill by describing it

      Say what you wish your agent could do, in your own words. It asks a couple of questions, writes the skill, and shows you a card to keep it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.2
    • Connect a service that is not listed

      Connect a service Archie does not list, using the web address of its API and your key, then write a skill that tells your agent which addresses to call.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • College

      Add each class's syllabus and your agent tracks the term: what is due this week, what you need on the final, and the school's own deadlines two weeks ahead.

      • On your computer
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.3.0

    Connections

    • What the first run says before connecting

      On the first run, before you connect a calendar or count your inbox, your agent says what it will read, where that goes, and how to disconnect it later.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Connect button under a reply

      When your agent says your calendar, your email, or an app is not connected, a button under its reply opens the Connections tab with the sign-in ready.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Connect an app's address for AI assistants

      Some apps hand out an address for AI assistants. Add it under Something else, and the tools that app offers join your agent's tools without an Archie update.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.3
    • What you can connect

      Google, Microsoft, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, Todoist, Fireflies, GoHighLevel, and any service you connect with your own key are reached directly from your computer.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Lights on your wifi

      Add Philips Hue, WiZ or LIFX lights from your own wifi, and your agent switches them over that wifi. The request never leaves your network.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • iCloud and other email

      Connect iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, AOL, Zoho or GMX mail with an app password you make on the provider's own site, plus its calendar where it has one.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.2
    • Choose Google Drive files

      Once your Google account is connected, choosing which Drive files your agent may read is a separate step, and you can leave it for later.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.12

    Your AI account and cost

    • Choose your AI company

      Your agent thinks with an AI account you connect: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, xAI, DeepSeek, or Mistral, or another service that works like OpenAI's.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • Ask your agent to switch AI company

      Ask your agent to use a different AI company, such as "use ChatGPT instead", and it switches, or says where to paste a key if you have none saved.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.5
    • A model on your own computer

      Archie can run your agent on a model on your computer through Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp, after checking that the model can use a tool.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.2
    • The spend meter

      Archie keeps its own estimate of what your agents' AI use has cost, this month and all time, by agent and by AI company.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.1
    • A monthly limit on AI spending

      You can set one monthly limit on what your agents spend on thinking, all of them together. When the month reaches it, routines and reading new mail and texts pause until the first. Your agent still answers when you ask, and reminders still go off.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.6
    • Response quality, and Use this for every skill

      Pick Economy, Balanced or Best for your agent's replies, and tick Use this for every skill so its add-ons use that setting too.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • Choose the models yourself

      Pick your own model for any of Economy, Balanced and Best from your AI company's list, and it runs in replies, skills and anything on a schedule.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.1
    • Another provider

      Connect any AI service that works like OpenAI's, such as Venice, by pasting its address, a model name and a key.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • When the AI runs out

      When the free credits or your plan's AI for the month run out, your agent says so once, with the ways to keep going, and keeps what you send.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Try again

      If the AI company has a passing problem, Archie asks it once more. If that fails too, the reply says whether anything was saved or sent, with Try again.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Working numbers out in Python on a Mac

      When an answer has to be exactly right, like a total, a loan payment or a spreadsheet's figures, your agent can work it out in a short Python program instead of in its head, and shows you the program under its answer.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.12

    Staying in control

    • Choose what your agent can do

      Switches decide what your agent offers, such as setting reminders or reading the web; turn one off and each message costs a little less.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0
    • What your agent will never do

      Your agent is awake only when you write, a routine's time comes, or it checks a mailbox you connected. It cannot run a command or text anyone.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • The crisis floor

      If you tell your agent you are thinking about hurting yourself, or someone is putting you in danger, it steps out of character and names where to get help.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3

    Privacy and security

    • Where your conversations go

      On your own AI account, what you write goes straight from your computer to that AI company, and Otian is not in the middle and keeps no copy.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • No analytics, and crash reports you can turn off

      Archie has no analytics service, and its version check-in and its crash and error reports carry your account ID but never anything you wrote, received, or asked for.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.3
    • The update check

      Archie checks for updates with a plain request that carries no version number, nothing identifying your computer, and no account.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.1
    • Where your keys are kept

      The keys you save for AI companies and services are kept in your computer's built-in password store, where we have no way to read them.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.1.1
    • The access record

      Archie writes down each time a saved key is used and each change to who or what can reach your agents, and shows if any line was changed.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.1
    • No list of the add-ons you install

      Adding an add-on raises its public popularity count by one, and we keep only the running total, never a list of which add-ons are yours.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.1
    • What Archie Mobile asks for on your phone

      Archie Mobile uses the camera, your photos, your files and the microphone only when you press to scan, pick, take or record something.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.1
    • Reset Archie

      Reset Archie erases your agents and your saved keys from your computer, disconnects every phone, and empties the phone mailbox.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • How long the phone mailbox keeps things

      Messages between Archie Mobile and your computer wait in a mailbox on Otian's server. The phone deletes each once read, and your computer clears leftovers a day later.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.2.5
    • What listens on your computer

      Nothing on the network can reach Archie. Only three things listen, on your computer and only while in use: a sign-in, the Google Drive picker, and the Computer control browser.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.1
    • An address your agent came up with waits for your yes

      Your agent opens a web page on its own only when the address came from you, from a page it already opened, or from a site you named in your message. An address it came up with itself, it shows you first and waits for your yes.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.5

    Plans

    • The plan with the AI included

      For $59 a month or $599 a year, Archie comes with $25 of Claude usage each month, so you need no AI account of your own.

      • On your computer
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.2.3
    • A 14-day trial on your own AI account

      When a computer has used its free credits, you can still try Archie for 14 days by connecting an AI account of your own.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • What Archie costs, on screen

      During a free trial, a strip at the bottom of the window says what Archie costs afterward, and the Account page's Your plan row says the same.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Ask what Archie costs

      Ask your agent what Archie costs or the cheapest way to keep going, and Archie answers from its own price list without asking the AI.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Add your AI account after buying a plan

      Buy a plan without the AI in it, and Archie asks for your AI account next, so your first agent starts as soon as it is made.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Free on your own AI account, 20 jobs a day

      Paste a key from an AI company and Archie opens for free, with every skill and routine, up to 20 jobs a day. A plan takes the limit off.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Not in Archie for Teams
      • Since 0.3.0
    • Your plan follows your Otian account

      A plan lives on your Otian account, so signing in on another computer gets the same plan.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.1.3
    • What happens when a plan ends

      A plan you stop runs to the end of the period you paid for. Nothing on your computer is deleted, and what opens next depends on your edition and key.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.0

    Archie for Teams

    • Archie and Archie for Teams on one computer

      Archie for Teams installs beside Archie as its own app, with its own data and its own keys, so one computer can run both.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.2.5
    • Move your agents into Archie for Teams

      When you hire, save a backup in Archie and open it in Archie for Teams, and your agents arrive with their knowledge, lists, routines and memory.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Team Starter pack

      A new Archie for Teams agent starts with Team Starter: a shared to-do list, a record of who took which job, web lookups, and a personality naming who it answers.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Write down who each teammate is

      When you add someone, write down their name and what they do, and an email or phone number if you like. Your agent then knows who is on the team, so asked to write to Dana it already has her address.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Choose what teammates can do

      On a shared agent you choose what the people you let in can do: ask it things, also add to and change its lists, or everything you can. In the middle setting a teammate can log a delivery or add a task to the agent's lists, and still cannot send your mail, change your calendar, or use the apps you connected.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.7
    • Owner, admins and teammates

      Everybody on an agent has a role. The owner is who the agent works for, and its routines report to them. An admin can change the agent and decide who is on it, the same as the owner, and whoever set it up can make the right person the owner.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.10
    • Add and edit people from your phone

      In Archie Mobile, under More, then Teammates, you can add someone, edit their name and contact details, take them off, or stop a waiting invite. You copy or share the invite message from your phone.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Teammates set and cancel reminders for themselves

      A teammate can ask your agent to remind them of something, and it reminds them in the chat they asked in, never on your to-do list. They can cancel their own reminders and nobody else's.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Your team this week

      Your agent's Dashboard lists your team: what each person does, how many messages they sent the agent this week and how many jobs those started, and when they last wrote. Press a name to read what they said.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • A teammate asking about the work gets their own entries

      When a teammate asks your agent about a list that says whose each entry is, they hear about their own entries and the ones with nobody named, and an entry they add is theirs. You still see every entry.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.8
    • What a teammate saved, told to you

      When someone on your team tells your agent something that adds to or changes one of your lists, you get a message saying what they saved. Under their reply, they see that you are told.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Archie for Teams only
      • Since 0.3.11

    Archie on your computer

    • Right-click an agent

      Right-click an agent in Archie to open it, start or stop it, rename it, change how it looks, or delete it.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.8
    • Keeps running with the window closed

      Close Archie's window and your agent keeps working. Archie stays running in the Dock on a Mac, or by the clock on Windows, until you quit it.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Opens at login

      Archie opens by itself, with no window, when you sign in to your computer, so your agent is answering again after a restart.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.9
    • Open Archie with a few keys

      By default, press Control, Shift and Space on a Mac, or Ctrl, Alt and Space on Windows, and Archie comes forward on your last chat, ready to type.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Archie in the Mac menu bar

      On a Mac, Archie has an icon in the menu bar at the top of the screen that opens it or quits it.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.11
    • Bring an agent over from OpenClaw

      Archie reads your OpenClaw agent's folder on this computer and shows you what it would make before it makes anything. Its personality, what it knows about you, its notes, its skills and its scheduled jobs become the new agent's.

      • On your computer
      • Since 0.3.1
    • When Archie is slow to open

      If Archie takes longer than usual to open, it says so. After a minute it offers Try again and Get help, and Get help starts an email to us with what it saw.

      • On your computer
      • From your phone
      • Since 0.3.11
